findings.statement: CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come almost entirely from neutrophils in Gubatan 2026 (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]); in Smillie 2019, which lacks neutrophils, the dominant lineage is T/NK, and this does not replicate (only GSE282122 agrees; Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 call it myeloid). After adjustment for cell composition the increase in inflamed mucosa is smaller but still significant, and stays an increase (verdict partly_composition) [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. It therefore reads mainly as a marker of neutrophil influx, with a smaller residual tissue increase; the adjustment may over-correct.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells (Smillie macrophages, inflammatory monocytes, DC2), and the myeloid attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122; in Gubatan 2026 neutrophil states also carry a large share of its transcripts. The composition-adjusted change is no longer significant (verdict composition) [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525], so the bulk rise mostly tracks myeloid and neutrophil abundance. This is not proof of pure influx, since activation of resident cells also raises lineage scores.

IL1B is myeloid in all four atlases (replicated, Smillie macrophages first, neutrophil OSM state prominent in Gubatan 2026), and its change loses significance after composition adjustment (verdict composition) [gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0732]. It behaves as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx rather than a stable intrinsic tissue change.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes first in Smillie; epithelial dominant in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, so replicated). Xenium sections attribute most transcripts to epithelium in inflamed tissue, and Visium deconvolution names the epithelial group as the in-situ source. The change stays significant after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], which supports a change inside the epithelium and makes it the clearest epithelial candidate in this list.

MMP1 is stromal, from inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie and in Gubatan 2026, replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122. Visium deconvolution names inflammatory fibroblast as the in-situ source, with neutrophils a secondary contributor; CosMx is at background. The change survives composition adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], so it is largely a change inside stroma.

CHI3L1 is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts), replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, but Gubatan 2026 calls it myeloid and neutrophil states contribute there, so attribution is mixed. The change stays significant after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], consistent with a tissue-level fibroblast change plus some neutrophil contribution.

IDO1 is myeloid (macrophages and DC1) in Smillie, replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, while Gubatan 2026 assigns it to epithelium (enterocytes), so the cell of origin is split; neutrophils make little of it. The change is retained after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], pointing to an intrinsic tissue induction.

TREM1 is myeloid in all four atlases (replicated) with a large neutrophil share in Gubatan 2026. Its change stays significant after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=TREM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.6621], so it is both an influx marker and a retained myeloid activation signal.

AQP9 is overwhelmingly neutrophil-derived in Gubatan 2026 per the neutrophil-share analysis. After composition adjustment its increase in inflamed mucosa is smaller but still significant, and stays an increase (verdict partly_composition) [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]. It is best read as a neutrophil-influx marker with some residual tissue increase.

CD274 (PD-L1) transcripts are mostly neutrophil and myeloid-derived in Gubatan 2026, and the change is retained after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978], suggesting a partly intrinsic checkpoint induction alongside influx.

HMGCS2 is epithelial in all four atlases (replicated) with almost no neutrophil contribution; its decrease persists after adjustment (verdict partly_composition) [gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.8548], indicating loss of epithelial metabolic function in inflamed mucosa rather than only a change of cell proportions.

caveats: Smillie 2019 contains no neutrophils, so its lineage call for neutrophil-dominated genes (e.g. CXCR2) is not reliable; Gubatan 2026 carries that information.
Composition adjustment can over-correct because lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate; a loss of significance is not proof of pure influx.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; Visium spot co-variation is weaker evidence than single-cell data, and MMP1 is at background on CosMx.
CXCR1 and several other top-ranked genes (CXCL1, MMP10, S100A8, S100A9, JAK2) were not individually profiled here.
